FOR 203.name: Field Dendrology
FOR 203.description: Establishes the basic skills of woody plant and tree species identification, for students pursuing natural resource management, ecology, or natural history studies.

FOR 350.name: Natural Resources Data Analysis
FOR 350.description: Statistical data analysis methods applied to natural resources problems.

FOR 200.name: The Profession of Forestry
FOR 200.description: Introduction to the profession of forestry and related career opportunities.

FOR 204.name: Silvics and Forest Dynamics
FOR 204.description: Tree life history, forest community characteristics, and stand development for sustainable forest management.

FOR 255.name: GPS and GIS Applications for Natural Resources Professionals
FOR 255.description: Applying GPS and GIS technologies for natural resource management, including spatial data capture and analysis.

FOR 266.name: Forest Resources Measurements
FOR 266.description: Collecting and analyzing quantitative data describing forest resources used in management decisions.

FOR 308.name: Forest Ecology
FOR 308.description: Community and ecosystem concepts including succession, productivity, nutrient cycles, and environmental factors affecting forest structure.

FOR 409.name: Tree Physiology
FOR 409.description: Physiological functions of forest trees including photosynthesis, water relations, and growth responses to environmental conditions.

FOR 410.name: Elements of Forest Ecosystem Management
FOR 410.description: Critically examines ecosystem management approaches for sustaining ecological integrity of forest ecosystems. Bulletin also requires 7th-semester standing, which the planner schema does not model directly.

FOR 421.name: Silviculture: Applied Forest Ecology
FOR 421.description: Methods to manage forested ecosystems for societal objectives, blending biodiversity maintenance with sustainable timber production.

FOR 430.name: Conservation Biology
FOR 430.description: Applies ecological and genetic principles to conservation issues, covering biodiversity protection, habitat fragmentation, and ecosystem restoration. Cross-listed with WFS 430.

FOR 450W.name: Human Dimensions of Natural Resources
FOR 450W.description: Addresses human needs and desires, from individuals to nations, for social, ecological, and economic benefits derived from natural resource decisions. Bulletin requires 6 credits of social/behavioral science gen-ed, which the planner schema does not model directly.
